title: The Hasse-derivative multiplicity oracle: characteristic-free exactness
content: The parent entry and its first child (-oq-01) show the ORDINARY iterated-derivative multiplicity test is defective in characteristic p: exact only for true multiplicities m < p, and overcounting WITHOUT BOUND the moment m ≥ p. This entry answers the positive question those negative results leave open: is there a derivative-style test that reports the exact multiplicity in EVERY characteristic? Yes — the HASSE derivative test. Replacing derivative^[j] by hasseDeriv j (the divided-power operator whose value does not carry the j! factor that collapses to 0 past p) yields a test that is exact with NO hypothesis on the characteristic at all. The capstone identifies rootMultiplicity a f as the least order at which a Hasse derivative fails to vanish at a — a correct multiplicity oracle over every field.
prerequisites: root multiplicity and the multiplicity Factor Theorem

title: HasseCertifies: the divided-power test, and it measures divisibility exactly
content: HasseCertifies f a n is the Hasse analogue of -oq-01's OrdinaryCertifies: the test certifies multiplicity ≥ n when every Hasse derivative of order below n vanishes at a. Unlike the ordinary value, the Hasse value carries no (j! : F) factor, so nothing collapses past the characteristic. hasseCertifies_iff_pow_dvd then reads the parent's Hasse criterion sub_pow_dvd_iff_hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero as a statement about the test: certifying multiplicity ≥ n is EQUIVALENT to (X − a)^n ∣ f, over any commutative ring and in every characteristic.

title: Exactness: the Hasse test never overcounts, in any characteristic
content: hasseCertifies_iff_le_rootMultiplicity: for f ≠ 0, HasseCertifies f a n ↔ n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f. Composing hasseCertifies_iff_pow_dvd with Mathlib's le_rootMultiplicity_iff, the Hasse test certifies multiplicity ≥ n exactly when n is at most the true multiplicity — it reports the true multiplicity and never a hair more, with NO characteristic hypothesis. This is the sharp positive counterpart to -oq-01's ordinary_certifies_all_of_char_pow_dvd, where in characteristic p the ordinary test certifies EVERY n once p ≤ m.

title: First nonvanishing order: vanishing below m, nonzero at m
content: The two halves of 'the true multiplicity is the first nonvanishing Hasse order'. hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero_of_lt_rootMultiplicity: below m := rootMultiplicity a f every Hasse derivative vanishes at a (from (X − a)^m ∣ f via pow_rootMultiplicity_dvd and the Hasse criterion; no f ≠ 0 needed). hasseDeriv_rootMultiplicity_eval_ne_zero: for f ≠ 0 the m-th Hasse derivative is NONZERO at a — because (X − a)^{m+1} ∤ f forces some Hasse derivative of order < m+1 to be nonzero, and every order below m already vanishes, so the offender is order m itself.

title: The capstone oracle: rootMultiplicity is the least nonvanishing Hasse order
content: rootMultiplicity_isLeast_hasseDeriv_ne_zero: for f ≠ 0, IsLeast {n | (hasseDeriv n f)(a) ≠ 0} (rootMultiplicity a f). Membership is the m-th derivative being nonzero; the lower-bound half is exactly the below-m vanishing (contrapositive). So the true multiplicity of f at a can be READ OFF as the first nonvanishing Hasse-derivative order — a correct multiplicity test over EVERY field, carrying no CharP hypothesis whatsoever. This is the positive resolution of the defect -oq-01 quantified for the ordinary derivative.

title: Head-to-head: Hasse stays exact exactly where the ordinary test diverges
content: hasse_exact_where_ordinary_diverges places the two tests side by side on the SAME polynomial in characteristic p. Take any f ≠ 0 with (X − a)^p ∣ f — the unbounded-overcount regime of -oq-01. Then the ordinary test certifies multiplicity ≥ n for EVERY n (pulled in directly from -oq-01's ordinary_certifies_all_of_char_pow_dvd), while the Hasse test does NOT certify rootMultiplicity a f + 1 (immediate from exactness). On the very polynomials where the ordinary derivative test runs away to ∞, the Hasse test still pins the multiplicity exactly.

title: The contrast realised on f = X^p
content: hasse_oracle_X_pow makes the head-to-head concrete on the canonical witness. Over a characteristic-p field the ordinary test certifies every multiplicity of X^p at 0, yet the Hasse oracle reads off the exact value: the least nonvanishing Hasse-derivative order of X^p at 0 is its true multiplicity p (via the parent's rootMultiplicity_X_pow). The same polynomial on which -oq-01's overcount_X_pow demonstrates unbounded ordinary overcount is pinned to exactly p by the Hasse test.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsLeast}\,\{n : (\mathrm{hasseDeriv}\,n\,X^p)(0) \neq 0\}\,p$ while the ordinary test certifies every $n$.
